16:08 Local Time, 10:08 GMT, 15:38 IST: Umpire Asif Yaqoob takes a reading on the lightmeter once again and the verdict is that the light has faded. The players once again go off the field due to bad light. Bad light was constantly a factor around 4pm local in Dhaka in the last Test and Sylhet being further on the eastern side of the country, this was always on the cards. Conditions being a bit overcast hasn't helped too. There's still a slight chance for light to improve. Let's wait and watch.

16:21 Local Time, 10:21 GMT, 15:51 IST: The floodlights are on and it is brighter on one side with the white fluffy clouds and dark on the other side. Chances of play look remote at the moment. Let's wait for official confirmation about stumps.

16:27 Local Time, 10:27 GMT, 15:57 IST: Nitin Menon is walking towards the players. Before that he removed one stump and put it on the ground when he walked out to the middle. Is that stumps? He seems to be telling the players something. And off walk the players inside. So that will be that. It's stumps on day 1. A pity that we didn't get more play in. But this is the eastern part of the country and light rarely gets better in winter here.

16:29 Local Time, 10:29 GMT, 15:59 IST: It has been a terrific recovery from West Indies after they were in some serious trouble early on at 27/3. Roston Chase at the toss reckoned that the surface looked dry hence he decided to bat. There was some moisture in the morning and the duo of Taskin and Hasan Mahmud made the new ball talk. Taskin in particular was highly impressive as he kept bowling in probing channels to keep the batters on their toes. He knocked King over with a beautiful inswinging delivery. Hodge had left a couple of tight back of a length deliveries but trusting the bounce on a pitch with early moisture backfired on him on the third occasion as his stumps were in a mess. Joshua Da Silva opened in Tests for the first time and he looked jittery. Taskin trapped him in front with a nip-backer to have the visitors wobbling.

The duo of Jangoo and Kevin Wickham though steadied the ship while the pitch flattened out nicely. Jangoo was positive from the onset while Wickham, the debutant, displayed good technique and temperament. They saw off the new ball threat, kept the scoreboard ticking and capitalised on the loose deliveries. Both raised their fifties and stitched together a 131-run stand. But, the short ball ploy perhaps got the better of Wickham as his feet hardly moved to a length delivery and he was cleaned up by Mahmud. Jangoo continued to flourish and brought up his century with a six and found an able ally in Greaves who batted solidly too. Bad light though came into play later in the day. It improved for a while as the players came back for 5 overs but it again intervened and forced the umpires to call it a day. Jangoo is struggling with cramps but continues to bat well. The game is nicely poised. Join us tomorrow to catch all the action from Day 2. Goodbye for now...

09:07 Local Time, 03:07 GMT, 08:37 IST: Day 2 -- It looked like the decision to bat had backfired on Chase & Co. yesterday. The West Indies were wobbling at 27/3 but what followed was a superb recovery from them. Jangoo and Wickham were the chief architects behind the rebuilding and they did a great job. Wickham couldn't kick on after raising a fifty on Test debut but Jangoo went from strength to strength and raised a terrific century. He was battling with cramps later in the day but a night's rest would have done him a world of good. Greaves has given him good support. The pitch eased out as the game progressed but the early morning moisture can definitely come into play this morning too. The second new ball is only 10 overs away so Bangladesh will count on that as well. Both Taskin and Hasan Mahmud made the new ball hoop and they will need to be at their best again. Another absorbing phase of play awaits us...

Talha Jubair | Bangladesh fast bowling coach: (On the outcome of the first hour of yesterday) We are happy because they have like four wickets down at the moment, but we are a bit unlucky, Hasan and Taskin. There's a lot of chances we dropped, like two catches we dropped. So if those catches were taken, could have been a different result. But happy with the effort the bowlers put in. But this morning, it's very crucial how we start. So we need to make sure the new ball is due in ten overs. So we need to be ready for that and looking for wickets, but at the same time, we need to contain the runs as well. (On what their bowlers could have done better?) No, I think the wicket looks very beautiful for the batters, because the wicket looks a bit on the slow side. But we bowled really well, especially our fast bowlers. But we need to continue this. But as I mentioned, we need to contain the runs before we think about taking wickets.
